cim_eredeti: DigiTec 2026 Brings Together Technology Leaders to Advance Armenia’s AI Ambitions
szoveg_eredeti:
YEREVAN — DigiTec 2026, Armenia’s leading technology conference, has opened in Yerevan, bringing together industry leaders, investors, entrepreneurs, and international experts to explore the future of artificial intelligence (AI).

Organized by the Union of Advanced Technology Enterprises (UATE), this year’s conference focuses on artificial intelligence and Armenia’s ambition to become a major global hub for AI innovation and infrastructure.

Speaking at the opening ceremony, UATE President Armen Kocharyan recalled that during DigiTec’s 20th anniversary celebration last year, organizers pledged not merely to reflect on two decades of achievements but to accelerate the industry’s development.

“Today, we are united around one bold ambition: to become a new global center for artificial intelligence,” Kocharyan said. “We are here to develop all five layers of AI together, connecting people, technology, capital, and markets in real time.”

He described DigiTec as a dynamic platform bringing together governments, investors, and businesses from Europe, the Gulf states, Central Asia, and North America to develop projects, attract investment, and expand operations.

According to Kocharyan, thousands of participants, including international guests, are expected to attend the three-day conference to explore Armenia’s technological achievements and future opportunities.

He emphasized that achieving these ambitions requires close cooperation between the government and private sector, supported by smarter regulations and reliable cross-border partnerships.

Kocharyan also highlighted Armenia’s investment in preparing the next generation of technology professionals.

“Through our public-private partnership involving Armath, the Armenian government, and the United Arab Emirates, we have established more than 650 engineering and robotics innovation centers across Armenia,” he said.

These centers provide children with free access to education in engineering, robotics, artificial intelligence, and entrepreneurship.

Kocharyan expressed confidence that Armenia is increasingly becoming an international crossroads for technology, investment, talent, and innovation.

“The next chapter of artificial intelligence will be shaped by those who choose to build together, right here in Yerevan,” he said.

NVIDIA Vice President Calls for Regional Cooperation

NVIDIA Vice President Rev Lebaredian, attending DigiTec for the third consecutive year, praised the progress Armenia’s technology sector has made.

Lebaredian noted that although technological development across the broader region remains relatively limited compared with Silicon Valley, Armenia possesses exceptional potential through its domestic talent and extensive global diaspora.

He pointed to Armenia’s historical role as a bridge between East and West, particularly along the Silk Road, as a foundation for future technological cooperation.

According to Lebaredian, DigiTec should aim to unite the entire region by engaging neighboring countries and international partners.

“By coming together, we can achieve far more than we could individually,” he said.

Lebaredian emphasized that Armenia, despite being the smallest country in the South Caucasus by population, can play an important role in developing different components of the AI technology ecosystem through regional collaboration.

“No country, regardless of its size, can accomplish everything alone,” he said. “If we distribute responsibilities, share knowledge, and connect our capabilities, we can create prosperity and peace. We cannot have a country without an economy.”

He also announced that NVIDIA has decided to significantly expand its activities this year, placing greater emphasis on AI infrastructure, which he described as essential to nearly every emerging technology.

Lebaredian noted that trillions of dollars are expected to be invested globally in AI infrastructure over the coming years. Securing even a small share of that investment, he argued, could substantially improve economic prosperity throughout the region.

He concluded with an invitation to international technology companies and professionals.

“Come to Armenia, make it your second home, build your technologies, exchange ideas, and share in the warmth and prosperity,” Lebaredian said.

Firebird Plans Major Expansion of AI Infrastructure in Armenia

Firebird co-founder Alexander Yesayan highlighted Armenia’s growing role in the global AI industry, pointing to the successful establishment of a major artificial intelligence center in Hrazdan.

Yesayan said the facility, inaugurated on August 8, had been an empty construction site just six months earlier.

“Today, it is the largest AI center in the region, developed in cooperation with partners such as NVIDIA and Dell, and already serving global customers such as Perplexity,” he said.

He described the project as evidence that DigiTec is more than a technology exhibition or conference.

“This is where ideas turn into real businesses,” Yesayan said.

While Armenia has traditionally built its technological reputation on the strength of its engineers, scientists, and skilled professionals, Yesayan stressed that talent alone is no longer sufficient in the age of artificial intelligence.

Developing a competitive AI industry also requires reliable energy supplies, advanced computing infrastructure, and large-scale data centers.

Yesayan announced that Firebird plans to expand its AI data center capacity in Armenia to more than 300 megawatts by the end of 2027.

Together with other projects underway in the country, the initiative aims to position Armenia among the world’s top 10 countries in AI computing capacity.

“Our goal is to make Armenia not only a destination for technology investment but also a trusted partner and bridge connecting Europe, the Gulf states, Central Asia, and the United States,” Yesayan said.

He added that Firebird is already expanding from Armenia into other emerging markets, strengthening the country’s position within the international technology ecosystem.

Technology Sector Accounts for Approximately 7% of Armenia’s Economy

Krisp co-founder Artavazd Minasyan emphasized the growing economic significance of Armenia’s high-technology industry, noting that the sector currently accounts for approximately 7% of the country’s economy.

“Armenia is a small country without major energy resources or access to the sea, but it possesses highly skilled professionals who solve complex problems and create value not only for themselves but also for the international community,” Minasyan said.

He attributed the development of Armenia’s technology ecosystem to a decade of sustained effort, cooperation, and investment.

Minasyan described DigiTec 2026 as an opportunity to assess those achievements while setting new goals for the coming decade.

“This conference is an excellent occasion to consider the next ten years and Armenia’s future accomplishments in information technology,” he said.

With artificial intelligence at the center of this year’s discussions, DigiTec 2026 underscores Armenia’s determination to strengthen its position in the global technology industry through investment, infrastructure development, international partnerships, and the cultivation of a new generation of innovators.
